item.title: [7] Microwave response of superconductors with paramagnetic impurities
item.description:
Last authors: Mehdi Zarea, J. A. Sauls

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of microwave response in superconductors with impurities, relevant to unconventional superconductivity.

Tags: #superconductivity #theory #microwave #impurities

Abstract: Dilute concentrations of paramagnetic impurities embedded in superconductors break Cooper pairs, create low-energy subgap quasiparticles that can impact the performance of superconducting microwave resonators and devices. The authors develop here the microscopic theory for the microwave response of superconductors with low-energy subgap quasiparticles and predict the low temperature Joule dissipation, anomalies in the London penetration depth, and frequency shifts of high- Q resonators. The authors show that microwave excitation of low-energy subgap quasiparticles gives rise to residual resistance of high- Q superconducting RF cavities.

Abstract: Rapid advances in nonlinear Hall transport provide new probes of quantum geometry, but transverse signals generally mix Hall and non-Hall contributions that are difficult to disentangle. item.title: [7] Unbiased large-N approach to competing vestigial orders of density-wave and superconducting instabilities
item.description:
Last authors: Grgur Palle, Rafael M. Fernandes

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory on competing CDW and superconducting orders, including altermagnetic phases; ties to user interests.

Tags: #theory #CDW #superconductivity #altermagnetism

Abstract: Vestigial orders are partially melted versions of ordered states stabilized by fluctuations of the order parameter. Observed in several quantum materials, their theoretical description has often relied on a large- N approximation that suffers from ambiguities due to multiple interfering channels. Here, the authors uncover the structural reasons for the ambiguities and from them derive a large- N prescription that removes the ambiguities, yielding unequivocal physical results. This prescription is then applied to multicomponent density wave and superconducting instabilities, where they find exotic vestigial phases describing spin-quadrupolar, charge-4 e superconducting, and altermagnetic orders.

item.title: [8] Spin-density wave of ferrimagnetic building blocks masking the ferromagnetic quantum critical point in NbFe2
item.description:
Last authors: A. Neubauer, C. Pfleiderer, F. M. Grosche, and P. G. Niklowitz

Authors: T. Poulis, G. Mani, J. Sturt, W. J. Duncan, H. Thoma, V. Hutanu, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Neutron scattering study of spin-density waves and quantum criticality in a magnetic system.

Tags: #neutronscattering #quantumcriticality #NbFe2

Abstract: Ferromagnetic quantum critical points can be masked by emerging modulated magnetic order. Here, the authors use neutron diffraction to show that the example of NbFe 2 provides the first case, where the masking modulated order is a longitudinal spin-density wave. The latter has a large-wavelength incommensurate modulation of its low average moment and is formed from ferrimagnetic building blocks with antiparallel ferromagnetic sheets. The findings can serve as a test case for magnetic quantum order-by-disorder models.
